dedupe_keys.name: international gnss service igs precise orbits clocks and reference products

description: The International GNSS Service is a voluntary federation of agencies, universities and research institutions that runs a global network of GNSS tracking stations and produces the reference products of satellite positioning. Analysis centres compute precise GPS and GLONASS orbits and satellite and station clocks in broadcast, ultra-rapid, rapid and final versions, together with station coordinates of the terrestrial reference frame, Earth rotation parameters, ionosphere maps, tropospheric delays, differential code biases and multi-GNSS (MGEX) products covering Galileo and BeiDou, plus a real-time service. Accuracy ranges from about 100 cm for broadcast orbits to about 2.5 cm for rapid and final orbits, with clocks near 75 ps; ultra-rapid products appear four times a day and finals every Friday with 12 to 19 days' latency. Coverage: global, from the 1990s. Format and access: SP3, CLK, SINEX, IONEX and TRO files from seven global data centres (CDDIS, IGN, BKG, ESA, KASI, SOPAC, Wuhan University); free, with citation of IGS requested and an Earthdata login for CDDIS. Caveats: products need GNSS expertise; formats and naming changed with long product names. Simulation uses: service performance baselines and space weather effects on positioning, and timing inputs for networks that rely on GNSS. Related records: FAA WAAS and Galileo performance reports give service-level statistics.
